n4aa70c19a79.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Rig Vedic worship?
o: Worship was conducted through hymns and yajnas in the open air
Temples and idols formed the normal basis of worship
Its principal aims included cattle, sons and victory
The cult of the domestic hearth was significant
n4aa70c19a79.x: Temples and idols were absent in Rig Vedic worship, which used hymns and open-air yajnas for material ends such as cattle, sons and victory.

n370049c66df.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no dates in the facts)
n370049c66df.s: In the Rigveda, the term 'Godhuli' denoted:
o: A wealthy man owning many cattle
The time of dusk, when cattle return
n370049c66df.x: Godhuli was the dusk time-measure when cattle returned; Gavyuti was a measure of distance, Gomat a cattle-rich man and Duhitri a daughter.

n1eeb92de665.s: In Rig Vedic irrigation, the term 'Kulya' referred to:
n1eeb92de665.x: Rig Vedic irrigation used wells (Avata) and canals (Kulya), with cattle-driven water lifts.

n49938fa0d8a.s: In the Later Vedic period, bali, bhaga and shulka were collected by the:
n49938fa0d8a.x: The Bhagadugha collected bali, bhaga and shulka; bali had by then become compulsory.

n8cd16fef712.s: In the Vedic period, a 'Hiranyakara' was a:
n8cd16fef712.x: Hiranyakara was a goldsmith; Takshan was a carpenter, Karmara a metal worker and Bhishak a physician.

n32b08053084.s: Which Rig Vedic god was called Purandara, 'destroyer of forts'?
n32b08053084.x: Indra, called Purandara, is the most mentioned Rig Vedic god with about 250 hymns.

n30b4bad6b89.s: In the Rigveda, the term 'nishka' denoted:
n30b4bad6b89.x: In the Rigveda nishka was a gold ornament or necklace; only later did it denote a unit of value. It was not a circulating coin then.

n374d56262a4.s: The Purusha Sukta occurs in which Mandala of the Rigveda?
n374d56262a4.x: The Purusha Sukta (Rigveda 10.90), a late addition, is in Mandala X and is the first statement of the four-fold varna.

n061c9d03b2f.s: Compared with the Early Vedic period, the position of women in the Later Vedic period:
o: Improved in assemblies but declined in rituals
n061c9d03b2f.x: Women's position declined in the Later Vedic period: they were excluded from Upanayana, rituals and assemblies.

n65e46a32de9.s: In the Early Vedic period, bali was:
o: A tax collected by a regular tax department
The king's fixed share of the produce
A voluntary offering by tribesmen to the rajan
n65e46a32de9.x: Early Vedic bali was a voluntary offering or tribute by tribesmen to the rajan and could include war booty; there was no regular tax system.

nindian-history-51-3.s: Which Vedic god was called Ritasyagopa, the guardian of Rita (cosmic order)?
nindian-history-51-3.x: Varuna guards Rita, the cosmic and natural order, and is therefore called Ritasyagopa.

ne8528970a42.s: Early Vedic society preferred sons, yet women could:
o: Receive education and take part in sacrifices and assemblies
Take no part in household religious rites
ne8528970a42.x: Early Vedic women received education, took part in sacrifices and assemblies and could own cattle; there is no evidence of land ownership.

n4866368e7ac.s: In Early Vedic agriculture, 'Langala' was a:
n4866368e7ac.x: Langala was a wooden ploughshare, while Sira was a plough drawn by bulls; iron was not used for the Langala.

ncb5f2b1d759.s: Marriage in Early Vedic society was largely:
ncb5f2b1d759.x: Early Vedic marriage was largely monogamous; adult marriage and choice in marriage were recognised and child marriage was absent.

na9eb9025d04.x: The early Vedic family was patriarchal, patrilineal and generally joint.

na03da87613f.s: Early Vedic texts mention slave women being given as gifts to:
na03da87613f.x: Dasa and Dasyu captives and slave women are mentioned, including slave women gifted to priests, though slavery was not the base of the economy.

nf91779d988f.s: Iron technology in North India emerged approximately between:
nf91779d988f.x: Iron technology in North India is dated to about 1000-800 BCE and was common at most Painted Grey Ware sites.

n6b4503250c3.s: Which god became supreme in the Later Vedic period?
n6b4503250c3.x: In the Later Vedic period Indra and Agni lost prominence and Prajapati became supreme.

n7ad063b2239.s: The Kurus were formed by the union of which two groups?
n7ad063b2239.x: The Kurus resulted from the union of the Bharatas and Purus; Kuru-Panchala, with its capital at Hastinapur, became the centre of Aryan culture.

n90a3f9149dd.s: Which Vedic text contains spells and charms against disease?
n90a3f9149dd.x: The Atharvaveda contains spells and charms; the Samaveda sets Rigvedic hymns to music and the Yajurveda gives ritual procedures.

nindian-history-56-12.s: In Vedic sacrifice, the Adhvaryu was the priest who:
o: Handled the practical, manual work of the sacrifice
Taught the Veda and Vedangas for a living
nindian-history-56-12.x: The Adhvaryu handled the manual work of the sacrifice; the Hotri recited hymns, the Upadhyaya taught and the Suta was the charioteer.

nea571693222.s: The legend of Videgha Madhava is narrated in the:
nea571693222.x: The Shatapatha Brahmana narrates how Videgha Madhava and Gautama Rahugana followed Agni Vaishvanara eastward from the Sarasvati.

n54ebaf7dfa5.s: In the Later Vedic period, rice was known as:
n54ebaf7dfa5.x: Rice (vrihi) became a chief crop with ritual importance, while barley continued to be grown.

n5b55be6a0ad.s: In the Later Vedic polity, the Sangrahitri was the:
n5b55be6a0ad.x: The Sangrahitri was the treasurer; the Senani was army chief, the Purohita chief priest and the Suta charioteer and herald.

n4b91a499b72.s: The largest number of oxen mentioned for yoking a plough in the Later Vedic evidence is:
n4b91a499b72.x: Ploughs were described as yoked with 6, 8, 12 and even 24 oxen, showing the growing scale of plough agriculture.

n965502748b4.s: Ochre Coloured Pottery is generally placed in which period?
n965502748b4.x: Ochre Coloured Pottery is post-Harappan and belongs to the second millennium BCE; the hallmark Later Vedic pottery is Painted Grey Ware.

n8b4b526fd25.s: Which Veda is associated with the Adhvaryu priest?
n8b4b526fd25.x: The Yajurveda gives ritual procedures in prose, is linked with the Adhvaryu and has Krishna and Shukla branches.

na0047a7f9c5.s: The Upanishadic thinkers criticised which tendency of Later Vedic religion?
na0047a7f9c5.x: Later Vedic worship became centred on elaborate rituals, which prompted the Upanishadic critique.

nb595070fcc9.s: In contrast to tribe-based Early Vedic society, Later Vedic society became:
o: Territory-based with agriculture and compulsory taxes
Urban and based on coined money
nb595070fcc9.x: The Early Vedic phase meant tribe, cattle and voluntary bali; the Later Vedic phase meant territory, agriculture and compulsory taxes.

nb0961bac923.x: Adichanallur is associated with urn burials and is not a Painted Grey Ware site, unlike Atranjikhera, Hastinapur and Bhagwanpura.

n4a434a96dde.s: Which Vedic texts are called 'forest texts' and give symbolic readings of ritual?
n4a434a96dde.x: The Aranyakas are forest texts giving symbolic readings of ritual; the Upanishads deal with Atman, Brahman, Karma and Moksha.

n325a799a64a.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no dates in the facts)
n325a799a64a.s: Which of the following belongs to the Later Vedic polity rather than the Early Vedic polity?
n325a799a64a.x: Ratnins were part of the Later Vedic polity; an elective chief, voluntary bali and strong assemblies marked the Early Vedic polity.

n06bec5f7117.s: In the Later Vedic period, royal succession usually favoured:
n06bec5f7117.x: Later Vedic kingship became generally hereditary, with succession usually favouring the eldest son, though traces of election continued.

nfd3e812ad8f.s: An Ashvamedha altar has been found at:
nfd3e812ad8f.x: An Ashvamedha altar has been found at Nagarjunakonda; early Andhra dynasties performed such rituals to proclaim sovereignty.

nc7a1888d767.s: Which Later Vedic royal ritual included a chariot race in which the king defeats his kinsmen?
nc7a1888d767.x: The Vajapeya included the chariot race; the Rajasuya was a consecration and the Ashvamedha a horse sacrifice asserting supremacy.

n6ffd485e399.s: Which Brahmana regarded the king as a protector of Brahmins?
n6ffd485e399.x: The Aitareya Brahmana regarded the king as protector of Brahmins; Brahmanical ritual monopoly supported royal legitimacy.

nddae75f5e49.s: In Later Vedic texts, the ruler of the eastern region was called:
nddae75f5e49.x: The eastern ruler was Samrat, the southern Bhoja, the western Svarat and the northern Virat.

n0c2beb42b76.s: Which Vedic assembly disappeared in the Later Vedic period?
n0c2beb42b76.x: The Vidatha disappeared, while the Sabha and Samiti continued under the control of chiefs and wealthy nobles.

ne8286a35eb8.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no dates in the facts)
ne8286a35eb8.s: Gargi's debate with Yajnavalkya is recorded in the:
ne8286a35eb8.x: The Brihadaranyaka Upanishad records Gargi's debate with Yajnavalkya.

nae3363ad9d4.s: In the Later Vedic period, varna increasingly came to be based on:
nae3363ad9d4.x: Varna became increasingly birth-based in the Later Vedic period, and gotra exogamy became important.

nf8564dc47c1.s: Which Satavahana ruler claimed to have protected varnashrama dharma?
nf8564dc47c1.x: Gautamiputra Satakarni claimed to have protected varnashrama dharma.

nd39d095a77d.s: Which ashrama involved gradual withdrawal from worldly life?
nd39d095a77d.x: Vanaprastha was gradual withdrawal; Brahmacharya was Vedic study, Grihastha household life and Sannyasa complete detachment.

nc0b15b72567.s: In Later Vedic sacrifice, which priest chanted the Samaveda?
nc0b15b72567.x: The Udgatri chanted the Samaveda; the Hotri recited the Rigveda and the Adhvaryu performed sacrificial acts.

n1b3a702e5cb.s: In the Later Vedic period, women lost the right of ____, the initiation ceremony.
n1b3a702e5cb.x: The status of women declined through loss of Upanayana, restricted education and exclusion from religious and public activities.

n39e457cf9c5.s: The proliferation of jatis is a feature of which period?
n39e457cf9c5.x: The proliferation of jatis was post-Vedic, including Gupta-era diversification; the later Vedic period saw birth-based occupation and rigid hierarchy.

na1b677750e7.x: Gotra literally means cow-pen; as an institution of descent from a common male ancestor it was established in Later Vedic times.

n39b126d80fb.x: Gotra exogamy prohibited marriage within the same gotra, operating alongside caste endogamy and sapinda restrictions.

nab777c7a3f3.s: Payment of a bride price characterised which form of marriage?
nab777c7a3f3.x: Bride price characterised Asura marriage; Gandharva marriage was based on mutual consent.

n5b8677d24b4.s: Varnashrama Dharma combines the varna system with the:
n5b8677d24b4.x: Varnashrama Dharma denotes the combined framework of varna and Ashrama.

n6fdfd6c561b.s: The earliest reference to the first three ashramas is found in the:
n6fdfd6c561b.x: The Chhandogya Upanishad first refers to the first three ashramas; all four are first listed in the Jabala Upanishad.

nindian-history-22-13.s: In the varna order, priestly functions belonged to the:
nindian-history-22-13.x: Priestly duties belonged to the Brahmanas; Kshatriyas were warriors and rulers, Vaishyas farmed and traded, and Shudras did manual work.

n6778383b1e7.s: Untouchability as a formal rule is associated with the:
n6778383b1e7.x: Later Vedic society discriminated against Shudras and Chandalas, but formal untouchability belongs to the post-Vedic Dharmasutras.

n4b622900ae1.s: Which ashrama was added later and was not well established in the Later Vedic period?
n4b622900ae1.x: Only Brahmacharya, Grihastha and Vanaprastha were prevalent in Later Vedic times; Sannyasa was added later.

nf5d5b35f98e.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no dates in the facts)
nf5d5b35f98e.s: Which Brahmana contains the first reference to money-lending?
nf5d5b35f98e.x: The Shatapatha Brahmana, the largest Brahmana, gives the first reference to money-lending and also mentions the Great Flood.

nab8661cc091.s: The word 'Andhra' first occurs in the:
nab8661cc091.x: The Aitareya Brahmana first mentions the Andhras, in the Sunahshepa story; the Rigveda does not mention them.

n2ad35031702.s: Which Mandala of the Rigveda is devoted to Soma hymns?
n2ad35031702.x: Mandala IX is the Soma Mandala; VI is linked with Bharadvaja, VII with Vasishtha and X with the Purusha Sukta.

n39334e7492b.s: The Shatapatha Brahmana belongs to the:
n39334e7492b.x: The Shukla Yajurveda has the Vajasaneyi Samhita and the Shatapatha Brahmana.

nafc37e3849f.s: How many hymns does the Rigveda contain?
nafc37e3849f.x: The Rigveda has ten Mandalas and 1,028 hymns, with Mandalas II-VII as its earliest core.

ndbff9268325.s: The Mahabharata is also known as the:
ndbff9268325.x: The Mahabharata is also called the Jaya Samhita and Satasahasri Samhita; the Harivamsa is appended to it.

n721fd667ebd.s: The Vaisheshika school of philosophy is associated with:
n721fd667ebd.x: Vaisheshika is associated with Kanada; Nyaya with Gautama, Sankhya with Kapila and Purva Mimamsa with Jaimini.

nd08cc41fa45.s: According to the Mahabharata, the Andhras sided with the:
nd08cc41fa45.x: The Mahabharata states that the Andhras sided with the Kauravas.

n406347dd148.s: The Rigveda shows similarities with which Iranian text?
n406347dd148.x: The Rigveda shows similarities with the Iranian Avesta.

n09c2501c532.x: Chandas is metrics; Shiksha is phonetics, Kalpa rituals and Jyotisha astronomy.

n4ee9f6c2f35.s: Vedic texts, regarded as 'heard', are classed as:
n4ee9f6c2f35.x: All Vedic texts - Samhitas, Brahmanas, Aranyakas and Upanishads - are Shruti ('heard') and called apaurusheya.

n219a28ad607.x: The Puranas are Smriti - later, legend-based works - whereas the Upanishads are Shruti.

necfea6fdecc.s: Which Sutras deal with the measurement and construction of altars?
necfea6fdecc.x: Sulba Sutras deal with altar construction; Grihya Sutras with domestic rites and Dharma Sutras with law and social practice.

n77d89a7b57e.x: The Upanishads are called Vedanta, the 'end of the Veda'; tradition counts 108, about 13 principal.

nbbc48e91997.s: Mitakshara, a commentary on the Yajnavalkya Smriti, was written by:
nbbc48e91997.x: Vijnaneshwara wrote the Mitakshara, a commentary on the Yajnavalkya Smriti.

nindian-history-53-8.s: The Prasthanatrayi consists of the Upanishads, the Brahma Sutra and the:
nindian-history-53-8.x: The Prasthanatrayi - the Upanishads, Brahma Sutra and Bhagavad Gita - forms the foundation of Vedanta.

nindian-history-53-15.s: Patanjali set out Yoga as a compact philosophical system in the:
nindian-history-53-15.x: Patanjali's system is in the Yoga Sutras; the Brahma Sutra is Badarayana's Vedanta text.

n04eca476ae2.s: The central philosophical teaching of the Upanishads is:
n04eca476ae2.x: The anti-ritualistic Upanishads teach Atman-Brahman identity and discuss karma, samsara and moksha.

n8baf9157dc8.s: Which branch of the Yajurveda contains mantras only?
n8baf9157dc8.x: The Shukla (White) Yajurveda contains mantras only, while the Krishna (Black) Yajurveda mixes mantras with prose.

nd3604e48b4f.s: The Gayatri Mantra occurs in which Mandala of the Rigveda?
nd3604e48b4f.x: The Gayatri Mantra is in the Third Mandala; the Seventh has the Battle of Ten Kings and the Ninth the Soma Pavamana hymns.

nindian-history-49-22.s: Cemetery R-37 at Harappa provides evidence of:
nindian-history-49-22.x: Cemetery R-37 at Harappa shows burial rites, while fire altars at Kalibangan and Lothal show fire rituals.

n5efc449be04.s: Which orthodox school of philosophy explains the world through atomism?
n5efc449be04.x: Vaisheshika is atomistic; Nyaya concerns logic and epistemology and Purva Mimamsa the authority of the Vedas, yajna and mantra.

nindian-history-49-21.s: Burial and post-burial rites are associated with which culture?
nindian-history-49-21.x: Burial and post-burial rites belong to Megalithic culture; yajna belongs to the Yajurveda, Purushamedha to the Shatapatha Brahmana and ceremonial chanting to the Samaveda.

n77fdbce9e85.s: Varuna, the upholder of Rita, ranked ____ among the Rigvedic gods.
n77fdbce9e85.x: Varuna, the ethically highest god, ranked third; Indra ranked first with about 250 hymns.

nindian-history-51-76.s: In Patanjali's Ashtanga Yoga, the fourth limb is:
nindian-history-51-76.x: Yama is the first limb, Niyama the second, Asana the third and Pranayama the fourth.

nf81c23e2aea.s: Which of the following limbs of Ashtanga Yoga belongs to the antaranga (inner) group?
nf81c23e2aea.x: Samadhi is antaranga; yama, niyama, asana, pranayama and pratyahara are the five bahiranga (outer) limbs.

nap-history-41-1.s: The Madhyamika school of Buddhism is associated with:
nap-history-41-1.x: Madhyamika is Nagarjuna's school; Syadvada is linked with Kundakundacharya, Dvaita with Madhvacharya and Purva Mimamsa with Kumarila Bhatta.

o: One of the six orthodox systems
nindian-history-51-4.x: Lokayata is a heterodox materialist school; the six orthodox systems are Sankhya, Yoga, Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Mimamsa and Vedanta.

nindian-history-61-2.x: Pashupata Shaivism was founded by Lakulisha.

n20d726d5c27.s: Criticising sacrifice as a mechanical activity, Upanishadic philosophy emphasised:
n20d726d5c27.x: The Upanishads criticised mechanical sacrifice and turned to meditation and instruction through a guru.

nindian-history-53-5.s: According to Upanishadic thought, the real aim of the soul is:
nindian-history-53-5.x: The soul passes through a cycle of birth and death, but its real aim is liberation (Moksha) from that cycle.

nindian-history-49-15.s: Which Vakataka king performed four Ashvamedhas?
nindian-history-49-15.x: Vakataka king Pravarasena I performed four Ashvamedhas, the Vedic royal horse sacrifice.

nbcc06647f7b.s: The Upanishadic identity of the individual self with the cosmic principle is expressed as:
nbcc06647f7b.x: The Upanishads identify Atman, the self, with Brahman, the cosmic principle.

nindian-history-53-3.s: Moksha, meaning liberation, was first discussed in the:
nindian-history-53-3.x: Moksha, meaning liberation, was first discussed in the Upanishads.

nb8928394f26.s: Which Rig Vedic god was associated with paths, herdsmen and cattle?
nb8928394f26.x: Pushan was god of paths, herdsmen and cattle; Rudra was the archer god of disease and mountains.

n635a09d9bb4.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the causes of the rise of heterodox sects?
o: Newly rich Vaishyas favoured the Vedic sacrificial religion
Mahavira and Buddha were both Kshatriyas
Vedic sacrifices consumed cattle needed for iron-plough farming
n635a09d9bb4.x: The newly rich Vaishyas wanted higher status and did not favour the Vedic sacrificial religion; the other three statements are correct.

n6e4070c6872.x: Gana-sanghas shared power in a clan assembly, while monarchies had a hereditary king.

n57b8ea34752.x: The Buddha attained parinirvana at Kusinara, a Malla centre; Mahavira died at Pava and the Shakyas were linked with Kapilavastu.

nindian-history-138-19.s: Panini's Ashtadhyayi mentions how many Janapadas?
nindian-history-138-19.x: Panini's Ashtadhyayi mentions 22 Janapadas, while the Anguttara Nikaya and Bhagavati Sutra list 16 Mahajanapadas.

ncbc54f00766.s: The rise of the Mahajanapadas and Magadha is associated with:
ncbc54f00766.x: The Mahajanapadas and Magadha were linked with the second urbanisation and the emergence of the first large Indian state.

nea6ed646761.s: Bimbisara received part of ____ as dowry from Kosala.
nea6ed646761.x: Bimbisara's marriage alliance with Kosala brought part of Kashi as dowry; he also allied with the Lichchhavis and Madra.

n0ba08c08fa2.s: Which was the only Mahajanapada situated south of the Vindhyas?
n0ba08c08fa2.x: Assaka was the only Mahajanapada south of the Vindhyas; eight of the sixteen lay in present-day Uttar Pradesh.

nf4174d0a9d1.x: Mahashilakantaka was a catapult; the chariot fitted with a mace was the Rathamusala.

ncc58d545c1b.s: Which Mauryan ruler is traditionally associated with Bhadrabahu in the southward spread of Jainism?
ncc58d545c1b.x: Chandragupta Maurya adopted Jainism and is traditionally associated with Bhadrabahu in its southward movement.

nindian-history-138-6.s: The Mahajanapada of Anga corresponds to the modern region of:
nindian-history-138-6.x: Anga lay in Bhagalpur and Munger; Kashi was around Varanasi, Koshala in Awadh and Malla in Kushinagar and Deoria.

nindian-history-138-13.s: The capital of the Ashmaka (Assaka) Mahajanapada was:
nindian-history-138-13.x: Ashmaka ruled from Potan/Potali; Gandhara from Taxila, Avanti from Ujjayini and Mahishmati, and Kamboja from Rajpur/Hatak.

n5eaf10127f2.s: Before its annexation by Kosala, Kashi was ruled by the:
n5eaf10127f2.x: Kashi, with its capital at Rajghat, was ruled by the Brahmadatta dynasty until Kosala annexed it.

nd9e5e0231b6.s: The Vatsa Mahajanapada was associated with which river?
nd9e5e0231b6.x: Vatsa lay on the Yamuna; Kosala was linked with the Sarayu, Avanti with the Sipra and Kashi with the Ganga-Varuna confluence.

n24f40abcbd7.s: Which Achaemenid ruler annexed Punjab and Sindh around 516 BCE?
n24f40abcbd7.x: Cyrus began the Persian invasions, and Darius I annexed Punjab and Sindh c. 516 BCE.

nf68155e346e.s: Magadha, Kosala, Vatsa and ____ were the four dominant powers of the Mahajanapada period.
nf68155e346e.x: Magadha, Kosala, Vatsa and Avanti were the four dominant powers of the period.

n9952b07ffab.s: Udayana, the hero of the Vasavadatta romance, ruled:
n9952b07ffab.x: Udayana ruled Vatsa and married Vasavadatta, daughter of Chanda Pradyota of Avanti; Bhasa's Svapnavasavadatta tells the story.

nf00e05cc5a8.s: The capital of the Vatsa Mahajanapada was:
nf00e05cc5a8.x: Vatsa's capital was Kaushambi; Shravasti was Kosala's, Champa Anga's and Ujjain Avanti's.

n14814a8c85f.s: Which of the following Mahajanapadas was a gana-sangha?
n14814a8c85f.x: Vajji, like Malla, was a gana-sangha; not all Mahajanapadas were monarchies.

nac44caeceea.s: Use of which language, placing religious teaching beyond common people, encouraged the rise of heterodox sects?
nac44caeceea.x: Sanskrit-centred religious practice, along with costly yajnas, animal sacrifice and dissatisfaction with ritualism, encouraged heterodox sects.

n6f66b819f87.s: Pataliputra stood at the confluence of the Ganga and the:
n6f66b819f87.x: Pataliputra was established at the Ganga-Son confluence; the earlier capital Rajagriha was protected by five hills.

na276dae2c2f.s: Which Nanda ruler was known as Ekarat?
na276dae2c2f.x: Mahapadma Nanda was called Ekarat; Dhana Nanda was the last Nanda ruler.

ne6b8192a4dc.x: Pukkusati ruled Gandhara, while Bimbisara ruled Magadha, Prasenajit Kosala and Udayana Vatsa.

n769e5ac929a.x: Alexander crossed the Indus in 326 BCE and died at Babylon in 323 BCE.

nindian-history-10-3.s: Who shifted the capital of Magadha from Rajagriha to Pataliputra?
nindian-history-10-3.x: Udayin moved the capital of Magadha from Rajagriha to Pataliputra.

n8dda0e3bfe3.shape: one-liner (NOT not possible: the original has no false statement)
n8dda0e3bfe3.s: Which technology made forest clearance possible in the Ganga plain, aiding the second urbanisation?
n8dda0e3bfe3.x: Iron tools facilitated forest clearance; with agricultural surplus, trade, coinage and state formation they produced the second urbanisation.

n9964952fd70.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Kaushambi – Fortified town on the Yamuna
n9964952fd70.x: Taxila, the Gandhara learning centre, stood at the junction of the Uttarapatha, not the Dakshinapatha, which was the southern route to the Deccan.

n9943d044aee.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no dates in the facts)
n9943d044aee.s: Coins bearing a ship-mast motif are associated with which Satavahana ruler?
n9943d044aee.x: Yajnasri Satakarni issued ship-mast coins; Satavahana trade centres included Kotilingala, Dhulikatta and Kondapur.

n8d61f2d37c4.s: Punch-marked coins were known as panas or:
n8d61f2d37c4.x: Punch-marked coins, called panas or karshapanas, carried symbols such as the sun, animals, trees and hills and followed standard weights.

n9d8af1ee860.s: In early Indian texts, the term 'Kusidin' meant a:
n9d8af1ee860.x: Kusidin meant a usurer; Setthi was a rich merchant-banker, Gahapati a wealthy householder and Vanija a trader.

n4e6c4d65d24.s: The Satapatha Brahmana uses which term for a usurer?
n4e6c4d65d24.x: The Satapatha Brahmana, which has the first reference to money-lending, calls the usurer kusidin; setthi was a merchant-banker.

na7fff69e5de.s: Dakshinapatha, the southern route to the Deccan, passed through:
na7fff69e5de.x: Dakshinapatha led south to the Deccan through Assaka, while Uttarapatha connected Taxila with the Ganga valley.

ndadbd0fdc05.s: Which inscription records guild deposits at fixed interest, showing that guilds acted as banks?
ndadbd0fdc05.x: Guild deposits at fixed interest recorded in the Nashik inscription show that guilds performed banking functions.

n0052fe1a3a3.s: Before issuing their own die-struck coins, the Satavahanas used inherited:
n0052fe1a3a3.x: The Satavahanas first used inherited punch-marked coins and later issued die-struck coins of lead, potin, copper and silver.

n9dfce17f41d.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no dates in the facts)
n9dfce17f41d.s: Which animals from the east strengthened the military power of Magadha?
n9dfce17f41d.x: Eastern elephants, nearby iron ore and Ganga-Son river transport contributed to Magadhan supremacy.

n4bb08fcc913.s: Which ruler of Magadha is associated with the Second Buddhist Council?
n4bb08fcc913.x: Kalashoka is associated with the Second Buddhist Council; Bimbisara conquered Anga, Ajatashatru defeated the Vajjis and Udayin shifted the capital.

nb97c3203c94.s: Greek writers referred to Dhana Nanda as:
nb97c3203c94.x: Greek accounts call Dhana Nanda Agrammes or Xandrames; he ruled Magadha at the time of Alexander's invasion.

nindian-history-139-20.s: Who is regarded as the real founder of the Magadha Empire?
nindian-history-139-20.x: Bimbisara was the real founder of the Magadha Empire; Ajatashatru succeeded him and Jarasandha belonged to the Brihadratha dynasty.

nindian-history-140-15.s: The Second Buddhist Council met at:
nindian-history-140-15.x: The First Council met at Rajgriha, the Second at Vaishali and the Third at Pataliputra; Ujjayini was Avanti's capital.

nindian-history-139-18.s: Jarasandha of the Brihadratha dynasty ruled from:
nindian-history-139-18.x: Jarasandha of the Brihadratha dynasty ruled from Girivraj, as the Sabha Parva of the Mahabharata relates.

nindian-history-140-20.s: Rajgriha, also called Girivraj, is identified with modern:
nindian-history-140-20.x: Rajgriha (Girivraj) is modern Rajgir, while Pataliputra is modern Patna.

nindian-history-140-12.s: Who built a fort at Pataligrama on the Ganga during the war with the Vajjis?
nindian-history-140-12.x: Ajatashatru fortified Pataligrama during his war with the Vajjis; his son Udayin later made Pataliputra the capital.

n68e8e8bc809.s: In contrast to the Vedic heartland, the society of Magadha was relatively:
n68e8e8bc809.x: Magadha's society was relatively unorthodox with little Vedic hold; iron, rivers, elephants and defensible capitals supported its rise.

nindian-history-140-11.x: Ajatashatru's other name was Kunika; Girivraj is another name of Rajgriha.

nd627faa6640.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no dates in the facts)
nd627faa6640.s: The Jain canonical texts, the Agamas, are associated with which language?
nd627faa6640.x: The Jain Agamas are associated with Ardhamagadhi, while the Buddhist Tripitaka is in Pali.

n6cdc4b8744f.s: Prolaraju's ____ inscription begins with a Jain prayer, showing the early Kakatiyas' Jain links.
n6cdc4b8744f.x: The early Kakatiyas were Jains; Prolaraju's Hanamkonda inscription begins with a Jain prayer.

nd400eb17f55.s: In Jainism, the ritual fast unto death is called:
nd400eb17f55.x: Sallekhana is the ritual fast unto death; Paryushana is a festival, Samvatsari the day of forgiveness and Pratikramana introspection.

n464a858562d.s: The doctrine of niyati (fate) is associated with the:
n464a858562d.x: The Ajivikas taught niyati; Jainism taught Anekantavada, Buddhism anatta and Charvaka materialism.

n313945dea05.x: Jiva is the conscious soul and Ajiva is non-conscious matter.

n2d5c247f698.s: The Jain basadi at Vaddamanu in Guntur was built by:
n2d5c247f698.x: Samprati, Ashoka's grandson, built the Vaddamanu basadi; Kharavela built a vihara near it and Indra III built Danavulapadu.

n65d7f3d5089.s: Prasenjit, a contemporary of the Buddha, was the king of:
n65d7f3d5089.x: Prasenjit ruled Kosala in the Buddha's time; Bimbisara was king of Magadha.

nbc32c1f602c.s: Regarding the authority of the Vedas, Jainism:
o: Accepts it as the ultimate religious authority
nbc32c1f602c.x: Jainism rejects Vedic authority and is non-theistic; it holds that souls exist even in natural objects.

n3c6c8c7d0d0.s: Which Buddhist doctrine contrasts with the Jain belief in an eternal soul?
n3c6c8c7d0d0.x: Jainism regards the soul as eternal, while Buddhism teaches anatta (no-self); both accept karma and rebirth.

nindian-history-51-29.x: Digambara means sky-clad; Digambara monks traditionally remain unclothed.

nindian-history-51-10.x: Parshvanath was the 23rd Tirthankara; Rishabhdev was the first and Mahavira the 24th and last.

ne710e424f4f.s: Samayasara, Pravachanasara and Panchastikaya were written by:
ne710e424f4f.x: These are works of the Digambara philosopher Kundakundacharya; Somadeva Suri wrote Yasastilaka Champu and Nitivakyamrita.

n2ed813b89ce.s: The historicity of which two Jain Tirthankaras is established?
n2ed813b89ce.x: Historicity is proved only for the last two, Parshvanatha (23rd) and Mahavira (24th); the first 22 are uncertain.

n4a82a34d8f3.s: The Jain doctrine that reality is many-sided and truth has many facets is:
n4a82a34d8f3.x: Anekantavada is the manifold nature of reality; Syadvada is conditioned predication and Nayavada the theory of partial standpoints.

n8e8516e03b7.s: Mahavira attained Kevala Jnana at the age of:
n8e8516e03b7.x: Mahavira renounced at 30, practised 12 years of asceticism and attained Kevala Jnana at 42; he died at Pavapuri aged 72.

n43861a90055.x: Mahavira was born at Kundagrama near Vaishali, son of Siddhartha of the Jnatrika clan.

n3292d5b3536.s: The milder vows observed by Jain householders are called:
n3292d5b3536.x: Jain householders follow the milder Anuvratas, which include non-injury, non-stealing, non-adultery, truth and non-possession.

n6396cc5df77.s: The fifth vow added by Mahavira to Parshvanatha's four was:
n6396cc5df77.x: Parshvanatha taught Ahimsa, Satya, Asteya and Aparigraha; Mahavira added Brahmacharya (celibacy).

n75fddf6d6c2.s: In Jainism, a fully liberated soul is called a:
n75fddf6d6c2.x: A fully liberated soul is a Siddha; Jina means 'conqueror' of passions.

nindian-history-51-11.x: Parshvanath attained Nirvana at Sammed Shikhar; Mahavira attained Kaivalya at Jrimbhik and Nirvana at Pavapuri.

nindian-history-51-77.s: Among the Jain Mahavratas, Asteya denotes:
nindian-history-51-77.x: Asteya is non-stealing; non-possession is Aparigraha.

n4fb344c43ca.s: Makkhali Gosala, once a companion of Mahavira, founded the:
n4fb344c43ca.x: Makkhali Gosala accompanied Mahavira for some years and later founded the Ajivika sect.

ne2467b9225a.s: The four forms of existence recognised in Jainism are Deva, Manushya, Tiryancha and:
ne2467b9225a.x: The four Jain forms of existence are Deva, Manushya, Naraki and Tiryancha.

nf9b98a28ceb.s: The cognizance (symbol) of Parshvanatha was the:
nf9b98a28ceb.x: Parshvanatha's symbol was the serpent; he renounced the world at 30 and his followers wore white.

n94b53da4f3c.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no dates in the facts)
n94b53da4f3c.s: The flight of a Jain monk to Hanamkonda from Rajaraja Narendra's persecution is recorded in the:
n94b53da4f3c.x: The Orugallu Kaifiyat records the monk's flight; Siddeshwara Charitra mentions Ganapatideva's persecution of Jains.

nbfed3ad3bbb.s: Who is regarded as the first Satavahana patron of Jainism?
nbfed3ad3bbb.x: Simuka (Srimukha) was the first Satavahana Jain patron; the Kalpa Pradeepa says his 52 army chiefs built 52 Jain temples.

n566c2ae57b4.s: The Eastern Chalukya Durgaraja built the Kathikabharana Jinalaya at:
n566c2ae57b4.x: Durgaraja built the Kathikabharana Jinalaya at Dharmavaram, not Danavulapadu.

n34ab2e9ee74.s: Which Jain leader is associated with the group that remained in Magadha?
n34ab2e9ee74.x: Sthulabhadra led the group that stayed in Magadha, while Bhadrabahu led the group that went south.

n8f2bcb8b7ab.s: The second Jain council was held in 512 CE at:
n8f2bcb8b7ab.x: The second council met at Vallabhi in 512 CE under Maitraka patronage, presided over by Devardhi Kshamashramana; the first met at Pataliputra.

n0a9e9eeb228.s: The Mahamastakabhisheka of the Gommateshwara (Bahubali) statue is held every:
n0a9e9eeb228.x: The Mahamastakabhisheka is held every 12 years at Shravanabelagola; the 88th was in February 2018.

n1635143ad6f.s: Jain writers produced the earliest important works and the first grammar of:
n1635143ad6f.x: Jains wrote the earliest important Apabhramsa works and its first grammar; their canon is in Ardhamagadhi Prakrit.

n5db173aada3.s: The Gommateshwara statue at Shravanabelagola was consecrated around 983 CE by:
n5db173aada3.x: Chamundaraya, a Ganga minister, consecrated the Bahubali statue at Shravanabelagola around 983 CE.

nde79d129068.s: How many Prakirnas does the Svetambara Jain canon contain?
nde79d129068.x: The Svetambara canon has 12 Angas, 12 Upangas, 10 Prakirnas, 6 Cheda Sutras and 4 Mula Sutras.

n011397a197d.s: According to tradition, Chandragupta Maurya ended his life by sallekhana at:
n011397a197d.x: Chandragupta, a disciple of Bhadrabahu, migrated south and ended his life by sallekhana at Shravanabelagola.

nd24aa72b502.s: Challenging caste hierarchy, Jainism stressed ____ over birth.
nd24aa72b502.x: Jainism challenged birth-based hierarchy, stressed conduct and action, and promoted vegetarianism.

n2943504b7a1.s: One factor in the decline of Jainism was its lack of:
n2943504b7a1.x: Lack of missionary zeal, along with loss of royal patronage, sectarian split, severe austerity and Bhakti revival, led to Jainism's decline.

n57bf09cb10e.s: The Buddha's mother Maya was a princess of the ____ clan.
n57bf09cb10e.x: Maya was a Koliya princess; Suddhodana was chief of the Sakyas, and Siddhartha was raised by Mahapajapati Gautami.

n59bca193dd5.s: Who recited the Vinaya Pitaka at the First Buddhist Council?
n59bca193dd5.x: Upali recited the Vinaya Pitaka; Ananda recited the Sutta Pitaka and Mahakassapa presided.

n6c77fa4a8cb.s: The Buddha attained enlightenment at Uruvela on the bank of the:
n6c77fa4a8cb.x: Enlightenment came at Uruvela (Bodh Gaya) under the Bodhi tree on the Niranjana.

ne76ef93106e.s: In the Eightfold Path, 'Sankappa' means Right:
ne76ef93106e.x: Sankappa is Right Intention; Samma-ditthi is Right View, Vaca Right Speech and Samadhi Right Concentration.

n97f26a31ecf.s: At what age did Siddhartha make the Great Renunciation?
n97f26a31ecf.x: Siddhartha left home at 29, accompanied by his charioteer Channa and his horse Kanthaka.

n2bc47f1383b.s: Vesak (Buddha Purnima) commemorates the Buddha's birth, enlightenment and:
n2bc47f1383b.x: Vesak marks the birth, enlightenment and parinirvana of the Buddha; the first sermon is not one of them.

n0f50a971685.s: How many of the eight Ashtamahasthanas lie in India?
n0f50a971685.x: Seven of the eight Ashtamahasthanas are in India; Lumbini is the eighth.

nindian-history-51-25.s: In Buddhist architecture, a Vihara was a:
nindian-history-51-25.x: A Vihara was a monks' residence; a Chaitya was a prayer hall and a Stupa a relic mound.

nindian-history-51-41.s: Who donated the Jetavana Vihara to the Buddhist Sangha?
nindian-history-51-41.x: Anathapindika donated the Jetavana Vihara; Vishakha built Pubharama and Bimbisara gave Venuvana.

n57388914c65.s: Which of the following was NOT a bar to admission into the Buddhist Sangha?
n57388914c65.x: Criminals, lepers and people with infectious diseases were excluded, but caste was no bar to admission.

na10391f9225.s: Before his enlightenment, Siddhartha's teachers were Alara Kalama and:
na10391f9225.x: Alara Kalama and Uddaka Ramaputta were his teachers; he then practised austerities with five ascetics for six years.

n820fc5f53fe.s: Vassa, the Buddhist rainy-season retreat, lasted:
n820fc5f53fe.x: Vassa was a three-month rainy-season retreat.

n84da9650d44.x: Jina, Kevalin and Nigantha Nataputta are all designations of Mahavira.

nf9d1fdb7fc9.s: In the Eightfold Path, Right Mindfulness belongs to:
nf9d1fdb7fc9.x: Right Mindfulness is part of mental discipline; ethics consists of Right Speech, Right Action and Right Livelihood.

nba8c34a0791.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no dates in the facts)
nba8c34a0791.s: The Mahaparinibbana Sutta belongs to which Nikaya?
nba8c34a0791.x: The Digha Nikaya holds the long discourses, including the Mahaparinibbana Sutta.

n9b028b4d0fa.s: Which Chinese pilgrim observed students memorising Nagarjuna's Suhrlekha?
n9b028b4d0fa.x: I-tsing noticed the memorisation of Suhrlekha, Nagarjuna's letter to a Satavahana king.

nindian-history-57-17.s: Which Buddhist text contains the rules and discipline of the Sangha?
nindian-history-57-17.x: The Vinaya Pitaka holds the rules of the Sangha; the Sutta Pitaka has discourses and the Abhidhamma the analysis of Dhamma.

n1c5f4d76540.s: Which place is regarded as the birthplace of the Mahasanghika sect?
n1c5f4d76540.x: Dhanyakataka is the birthplace of the Mahasanghika sect; Mahadeva, who led the Mahasanghikas, began Chaitikavada in Andhra.

n85b6b5792ce.s: Which form of Buddhism seeks salvation through mantras, mudras and mandalas?
n85b6b5792ce.x: Vajrayana uses mantras, mudras and mandalas; the Arhat ideal belongs to Hinayana and the Bodhisattva ideal to Mahayana.

n779b5d6c964.s: How many of the eighteen early Buddhist sects existed in Andhra?
n779b5d6c964.x: Nine of the eighteen early Buddhist sects existed in Andhra.

n99b2a96861c.s: The Purvasaila branch of the Chaityakas was centred at:
n99b2a96861c.x: Purvasaila was at Amaravati, Aparasaila at Nagarjunakonda and Siddhadhika at Gudivada.

n7a5dbe12efc.s: Ashoka's stupa at Sanchi was encased in stone during the ____ period.
n7a5dbe12efc.x: Built by Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE, Sanchi was encased in stone under the Shungas and became a World Heritage Site in 1989.

nb796d4b128e.x: Buddhaghosha, born near Guntur, composed the Visuddhimagga at Anuradhapura, not Amaravati.

n94eecd61081.x: Ashvaghosha wrote Buddhacharita and Saundarananda; Abhidharmakosa is Vasubandhu's and Tarkajvala Bhavaviveka's.

n881b160f7e5.s: Kumaralata is associated with which Buddhist school?
n881b160f7e5.x: Kumaralata is associated with Sautrantika, which relies on the Suttas; Asanga and Vasubandhu are linked with Yogachara.

nd34249fa329.s: The First Buddhist Council at Rajagriha was held under the patronage of:
nd34249fa329.x: The First Council met at Rajagriha under Ajatashatru; the Second met at Vaishali under Kalashoka.

n2fd4040576b.s: Besides maritime trade, Buddhism reached Central Asia and China along the Kushan-era:
n2fd4040576b.x: The Kushan-era Silk Route and sea trade spread Buddhism abroad; Turkish raids contributed to its decline in India.

n7968eb9cca9.s: The Dhammapada is part of which Nikaya?
n7968eb9cca9.x: The Khuddaka Nikaya includes the Dhammapada, Theragatha, Therigatha and Jatakas.

n414c9c54f07.x: Yamaka and Kathavatthu belong to the Abhidhamma, described as having seven books; Patimokkha belongs to the Vinaya Pitaka.

n1aa52894f39.s: Which of the following Buddhist works belongs to the Sanskrit group rather than Pali literature?
n1aa52894f39.x: Divyavadana is a Sanskrit work, whereas Dipavamsa, Mahavamsa and Visuddhimagga are Pali works.

nindian-history-51-27.s: The Guhyasamaja is an important text of which Buddhist school?
nindian-history-51-27.x: The Guhyasamaja is an important tantric text of Vajrayana, which flourished from the eighth century.

n9618d721b0f.s: The replacement of Pali by which language is associated with the decline of Buddhism?
n9618d721b0f.x: Replacement of Pali by Sanskrit, corruption of the Sangha, Brahmanical-Bhakti revival and loss of royal patronage are associated with decline.

nddf1903d003.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Ikshvaku phase of Buddhism in Andhra?
o: According to the Mahavamsa, Mahadeva Bhikshu brought Buddhism from Sri Lanka to Andhra
Veerapurushadatta rebuilt the Nagarjunakonda Maha Chaitya
A trampled Shivalinga sculpture reflects Veerapurushadatta's hostility to Saivism
nddf1903d003.x: The Mahavamsa says Mahadeva Bhikshu took Buddhism from Andhra to Sri Lanka, not the other way round.

nfce32a96a56.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no dates in the facts)
nfce32a96a56.s: Amaravati is identified with the ancient city of:
nfce32a96a56.x: Amaravati is ancient Dhanyakataka on the Krishna; its stupa, the largest in Andhra Pradesh, was identified by Colin Mackenzie in 1797.

n933dc119aba.s: The Buddhist centre of Odantapuri is associated with the Pala ruler:
n933dc119aba.x: Odantapuri is associated with Gopala, while Vikramashila is linked with Dharmapala.

n0b8d8e87a2c.s: Nagarjunakonda was the capital of the:
n0b8d8e87a2c.x: Nagarjunakonda, now an island in the Nagarjuna Sagar, was an Ikshvaku capital with over thirty stupas and a Sinhala vihara.

nindian-history-76-3.s: The monolithic Kailasa temple at Ellora was carved under the:
nindian-history-76-3.x: Ellora's Kailasa temple was carved under the Rashtrakutas; Ajanta belongs to the Satavahana and Vakataka phases.

nindian-history-76-11.s: Which cave complex contains Buddhist, Hindu and Jain caves?
nindian-history-76-11.x: Ellora mixes Buddhist, Hindu and Jain caves; Ajanta and Kanheri are Buddhist and Elephanta is Shaiva.

n5ff5996e8d0.s: The Udayagiri-Khandagiri caves of Kharavela in Odisha are:
n5ff5996e8d0.x: Udayagiri-Khandagiri are Jain caves of Kharavela; Karle and Guntupalli are Buddhist sites.

ne46aabf7e85.s: The Buddhist site of Sankaram (Bojjannakonda) was brought to notice in 1906 by:
ne46aabf7e85.x: Alexander Rea found Sankaram in 1906; Gidugu Ramamurthy found Salihundam in 1919.

nindian-history-76-20.s: Which of the following cave sites has Ashokan inscriptions?
nindian-history-76-20.x: Barabar has Ashokan inscriptions; Kanheri has over 100 caves and Bagh shows scenes of public life.

n1734813207b.s: The Bagh caves are located in:
n1734813207b.x: Bagh is in Madhya Pradesh; Bhaja is in Maharashtra, Udayagiri-Khandagiri in Odisha and Sittanavasal in Tamil Nadu.

n29771423195.s: In a stupa, the central mast is called the:
n29771423195.x: The yashti is the central mast; the anda is the hemispherical mound, the vedika the railing and toranas the gateways.

nf1c571457e8.x: Sriparvata is Nagarjunakonda, while Dhanyakataka is Amaravati.

nc197e525974.s: In early Buddhist art, the Dharmachakra symbolises the Buddha's:
nc197e525974.x: The Dharmachakra represents the first sermon; the horse Kanthaka represents renunciation and footprints represent parinirvana.

nindian-history-14-18.s: Somapura Mahavihara at Paharpur was founded by:
nindian-history-14-18.x: The Pala king Dharmapala founded Somapura Mahavihara at Paharpur, now in Bangladesh.

nap-history-24-12.s: The eight Bhairavakonda caves are located in which district?
nap-history-24-12.x: The Bhairavakonda caves, eight in number, are in Nellore district.

nindian-history-26-2-35.x: Kondaveedu was a Reddy kingdom capital; Warangal was the Kakatiya capital and Penukonda a Vijayanagara stronghold.

nindian-history-76-16.s: The largest and most evolved Hinayana chaitya hall in India is at:
nindian-history-76-16.x: The Karla chaitya near Lonavala, cut in the Satavahana period, is the largest and most developed Hinayana chaitya.

n70a43b0ec9c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the heterodox schools' views on karma?
o: Jainism: karma is material bondage removable by penance
n70a43b0ec9c.x: Charvaka does not accept karma as a determining force of rebirth; the other three views are correctly stated.

n8fffaf63609.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no dates in the facts)
n8fffaf63609.s: The Ajivikas held that human thoughts and actions were:
n8fffaf63609.x: The Ajivikas were determinists: actions were fixed before birth, there was no free will, and karma could not alter destiny.

n2cc214dc73d.x: Ajivika ascetics, who practised extreme austerities, were often called Sudra sannyasins; the sect had no caste discrimination.

n0f387a8271d.s: According to the Charvaka school, the soul is:
o: An eternal entity that survives death
n0f387a8271d.x: Charvaka identifies the conscious body with the soul and denies that any separate soul survives death.

n3ebeabd77cd.s: The Charvaka school is also known as:
n3ebeabd77cd.x: Charvaka is also called Lokayata and Barhaspatya; Niyativada is the Ajivika doctrine of Makkhali Gosala.

ndf8d723cb30.s: The only pramana (means of valid knowledge) accepted by the Charvaka school is:
ndf8d723cb30.x: Charvaka accepts only perception, while Nyaya accepts perception, inference, comparison and testimony.

n3404999f615.s: For about how many years was Makkhali Gosala Mahavira's companion?
n3404999f615.x: Gosala spent about six years as Mahavira's companion before breaking away to lead the Ajivikas.

n206c84e8108.s: Alexander divided his conquered Indian territory into how many parts under Greek governors?
n206c84e8108.x: The conquered area was divided into three parts under Greek governors; most submitted states were returned to their rulers.

nindian-history-39-17.s: Massaga was the capital of the:
nindian-history-39-17.x: Massaga was the Ashvaka capital; Alexander fought Porus at the Jhelum.

n8e9388e203b.s: The Kharosthi script, derived from Aramaic, was written:
n8e9388e203b.x: Kharosthi was written from right to left; Persian influence also showed in Aramaic edicts and the satrapy system.

n137f80d1860.s: Alexander set up twelve large stone altars on the northern bank of the:
n137f80d1860.x: Alexander raised twelve altars on the northern bank of the Beas, then withdrew down the Indus while Nearchus led the fleet.

n7d67c75f108.s: Alexander entered India in 326 BC through the:
n7d67c75f108.x: Alexander crossed the Hindu Kush in 327 BC and entered India through the Khyber Pass in 326 BC.

n8c3e0a106a1.s: After his defeat at the Hydaspes in 326 BC, Porus:
o: Had his kingdom restored and later enlarged
n8c3e0a106a1.x: Porus was defeated but not executed; Alexander restored and later enlarged his kingdom.

nindian-history-39-13.s: Which Indian ruler was an ally of Alexander?
nindian-history-39-13.x: Indian allies such as Ambhi, along with political disunity and a superior army, helped Alexander.

nindian-history-39-14.s: The territory of Porus extended between the Jhelum and the:
nindian-history-39-14.x: Porus (Puru) ruled between the Jhelum and Chenab, and his kingdom was restored after his defeat.

nindian-history-39-15.s: Alexander's return point in India was:
nindian-history-39-15.x: Alexander invaded in 326 BC, left in 325 BC and returned via Patala (Paatal).

nindian-history-17-3.s: The Kalinga War, the turning point in Ashoka's life, was fought in:
nindian-history-17-3.x: The bloodshed of the Kalinga War (261 BC) turned Ashoka to Buddhism and the policy of Dhamma.

nac7b7de0651.s: Besides war weariness and homesickness, Alexander's army refused to go beyond the Beas from fear of the army of the:
nac7b7de0651.x: War weariness, homesickness, disease and fear of the Nanda army caused the refusal.

n886a87d16e8.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Megasthenes' Indica?
o: It contains uncritical folklore such as the gold-digging ants
It correctly reported that slavery was widespread in Mauryan India
Strabo, following Megasthenes, said Indians did not know writing
Its claim of no slavery is contradicted by the Arthashastra and Ashokan edicts
n886a87d16e8.x: Megasthenes claimed there was no slavery in India, a claim contradicted by the Arthashastra and Ashokan edicts that mention dasas.

nbd10708bf1d.s: Megasthenes described Indian society as divided into how many classes?
nbd10708bf1d.x: Megasthenes described seven classes and noted endogamy and hereditary occupations; this was not the fourfold varna scheme.

n6bf4182da2f.s: According to Rudradaman I's Junagadh inscription, the Sudarshana lake was built in Chandragupta Maurya's reign by the governor:
n6bf4182da2f.x: The Junagadh inscription (c. 150 CE) records that governor Pushyagupta built the Sudarshana lake under Chandragupta Maurya.

nb26b0603797.s: The Arthashastra was rediscovered at Mysore in 1905 by:
nb26b0603797.x: R. Shamasastry rediscovered the Arthashastra in 1905 and it was published in 1909; it has 15 books called adhikaranas.

nbee32036a8c.s: With reference to Chandragupta Maurya's expansion, which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Seleucus – Ceded four provinces up to Afghanistan
Mamulanar – Greek chronicler of the Mauryas
Greek satraps – Expelled from the north-west
nbee32036a8c.x: Mamulanar was a Tamil poet who referred to the Mauryas' southward expansion, not a Greek chronicler.

ned09a126a8f.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no dates in the facts)
ned09a126a8f.s: Who handled the later Taxila revolt during Ashoka's reign?
ned09a126a8f.x: Susima failed against the first Taxila revolt, Ashoka was then sent, and Kunala handled a later revolt during Ashoka's reign.

n115af3d4833.s: Which was the first empire to unite most of the Indian subcontinent?
n115af3d4833.x: The Mauryan Empire first united most of the subcontinent, covering present-day India, Pakistan, Bangladesh and parts of Afghanistan, and reached the Deccan.

n5f91b9e106f.s: Chanakya, author of the Arthashastra, was also known as Kautilya and:
n5f91b9e106f.x: Chanakya was also called Kautilya and Vishnugupta; he guided Chandragupta and is associated with Taxila.

n79e1f8878d7.s: Brahmagiri, Siddapura and Jatinga-Rameshwara, marking the southern reach of the Mauryan Empire, are in present-day:
n79e1f8878d7.x: The Mauryan southern reach extended into Karnataka, marked by these edict sites; the Tamil kingdoms lay outside the empire.

ncc48f35f98f.s: Which Ashokan site in Kurnool district has both major and minor edicts?
ncc48f35f98f.x: Yerragudi has both major and minor edicts; Rajula Mandagiri, also in Kurnool, has only a minor edict.

nindian-history-51-42.s: The Barabar and Nagarjuni caves were given to the monks of which sect?
nindian-history-51-42.x: The Barabar and Nagarjuni caves were given to the Ajivikas, patronised by Ashoka and Dasharatha.

na61a1f42605.x: Bindusara, son of Chandragupta and Durdhara, was born Simhasena; Ashoka's mother was Subhadrangi.

n7056e0b8cec.s: Deimachus was sent to Bindusara's court by:
n7056e0b8cec.x: Antiochus I sent Deimachus to Bindusara; Ptolemy II sent Dionysius, and Seleucus I sent Megasthenes to Chandragupta.

nb8d1a95f153.s: Of Bindusara's requests to Antiochus I, which one could not be met?
nb8d1a95f153.x: Antiochus sent sweet wine and dried figs, but a philosopher could not be sold or sent as a commodity.

nindian-history-76-7.s: The Lomas Rishi cave, a Mauryan cave linked to the Ajivikas, is in the ____ Hills of Bihar.
nindian-history-76-7.x: Lomas Rishi is one of the Barabar Hill caves in Bihar, famous for its carved facade.

nindian-history-14-10.s: Takshashila (Taxila), the ancient centre of learning, was located in:
nindian-history-14-10.x: Takshashila lay in Gandhara, in present north-west Pakistan, and was a famous centre of learning.
